If $d>1$, then $\abs{x-d}=d-x\ge1-x=\abs{x-1}$ for $x\in[-1,1]$, so $\mathcal J(d)\le\mathcal J(1)=\pi+2\log(1+\sqrt2)<\pi+4\log2$. For \eqref{eq:rearrange}, write $g(y)=\int_0^\infty\1\{g(y)>\sigma\}\dd\sigma$ and $h(y)=\int_0^\infty\1\{h(y)>\tau\}\dd\tau$. For $\sigma,\tau\ge0$ the sets $\{g>\sigma\}$ and $\{h>\tau\}$ are intervals centred at $0$, possibly empty or all of $\R$, and $\{y:h(y-b)>\tau\}$ is the translate of the second by $b$. The length of the intersection of two intervals is at most the length of the shorter one, with equality when they have the same centre. Hence $\abs{\{g>\sigma\}\cap(b+\{h>\tau\})}\le\abs{\{g>\sigma\}\cap\{h>\tau\}}$, and integrating over $\sigma$ and $\tau$ with Tonelli's theorem gives \eqref{eq:rearrange}.
